questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Five containers weigh 9, 11, 14, 18, 24 kg. A loading bay accepts exactly two whose combined weight is exactly 33 kg. The heavier selected container is loaded first. Which weight is loaded second?
questions.explanation: Testing pairs against the capacity leaves 24 + 9 = 33. In descending weight order the second is 9 kg.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A lamp is already on. Each pulse reverses its state. It receives 16 pulses before a pause, then 14 more pulses. During maintenance the technician manually toggles it once and disconnects it before any further pulse. What was its state immediately before the manual toggle and immediately afterwards?
questions.explanation: The total number of automatic toggles is 30. Each pair cancels. The manual toggle then reverses the state once more.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question:
Exactly one of Bela, Dev, Ela is assigned a report, and exactly 2 of the following claims are true.
1. Bela is assigned the report.
2. Ela is assigned the report.
3. Ela is not assigned the report.
Who receives the report?
questions.explanation: Test the three possible recipients. Assigning the report to Bela makes 2 claims true; assigning it to Dev makes 1 claims true; assigning it to Ela makes 1 claims true. Only Bela yields the required count.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: An audit reviews 36 requests. A request can pass only if both its date and fare are verified. All requests with verified fares have reference codes. Exactly 9 requests lack a code and 11 requests lack date verification. The two groups overlap in two cases. What is the largest possible number of passes?
questions.explanation: Any request without a code lacks fare verification and therefore fails. The union of the two groups is 9 + 11 − 2 = 18 requests. At most 36 − 18 can pass, and that is possible if all other requests meet both requirements.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Five applicants Farah, Gita, Hema, Indu and Jaya are each on at least one of two lists. List X has three names and List Y has three names. X includes Farah and Gita; Y includes Hema and Indu. Both lists exclude the two names already given for the other list. Who must appear on both?
questions.explanation: The given members are exclusive. The only remaining applicant, Jaya, must fill the third place on both lists.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A surveyor starts facing north, goes 16 m forward, turns left and goes 9 m, then turns left again and goes 13 m. Ignoring obstacles, which displacement from the start is correct?
questions.explanation: The first and third walks are opposite, leaving 16 − 13 = 3 m along the original heading. The middle walk is to the left of the starting direction.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Exactly two of Farah, Gita, Hema and Indu are on leave. Farah is on leave if and only if Hema is on leave. Indu is working. The two people at work must cover reception and records, one duty each. Indu covers records. Who covers reception?
questions.explanation: Because Indu is working and exactly two people are on leave, the paired leave status must put Farah and Hema on leave. The working pair is Gita and Indu.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Team P inspected 18 boxes and team Q inspected 9 boxes. Exactly 11 of all inspected boxes were rejected. Each team inspected a disjoint set. What is the minimum possible number of rejections from P?
questions.explanation: At most 9 rejections can come from Q because Q inspected only 9. That leaves at least 2 among P. The minimum is attainable if every Q box was rejected.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A committee selects exactly two of reports Farah, Gita, Hema and Indu. Selecting Farah forces Hema. Selecting Indu rules out Hema. New rules also forbid choosing Gita together with Hema, and forbid choosing Gita together with Indu. Which pair can be selected?
questions.explanation: Any pair containing Farah must also contain Hema. Without Farah, all three possible pairs among Gita, Hema and Indu breach a prohibition. The single valid pair is Farah–Hema.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A manager expects staggered break times to reduce the longest queue without adding staff. What must the argument assume?
options: The total daily number of customers will fall.
The change leaves enough staff available during at least part of the existing peak.
Every staff member takes the same length of break.
The average queue outside the peak is longer than during it.
questions.explanation: Staggering could help only if it changes available service capacity when the longest queue forms.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A supervisor claims that whenever a report is read, an acknowledgement is received. Which observation is sufficient to refute the claim?
options: An unread report has no acknowledgement.
A read report has two acknowledgements.
A report receives an acknowledgement before its author checks the log.
One read report has no acknowledgement.
questions.explanation: The claim is R → A. The only direct counterexample is R true and A false.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Which order satisfies every clue, from position 1 to position 5?
questions.explanation: Checking the stated restrictions leaves only Asha → Charu → Esha → Bina → Deepa. Asha → Deepa → Charu → Esha → Bina violates clue 1. Charu → Esha → Bina → Deepa → Asha violates clue 4. Deepa → Asha → Charu → Esha → Bina violates clue 1.
questions.passage:
Five interviews take place on Monday through Friday, one per day. Positions 1–5 are Monday–Friday.
1. Bina is interviewed immediately before Deepa.
2. Charu is interviewed two days before Bina.
3. Esha is interviewed after Charu but before Bina.
4. Asha is earlier than Charu.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: If clue 1 is dropped and all other clues still apply, how many orders are possible?
questions.explanation: Retain all clues except 1. The remaining constraints admit 4 distinct permutations, including the original order. Count arrangements with position 1 fixed before moving to the next permitted first item.
questions.passage:
Five colleagues are assigned one each to desks numbered 1–5 from left to right.
1. Lata works at desk 3.
2. Kiran works two desks to the right of Lata.
3. Meena has a lower desk number than Pia.
4. Pia is not immediately to the left of Kiran.
5. Nila sits to the right of Meena.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Between 7:00 and the first overlap after it, when is the smaller angle between the clock hands 17.5°?
questions.explanation: On this side of the overlap the separation is 30 × 7 − 5.5m. Set that equal to 17.5 and solve for m = 35.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A register is inspected on a Saturday. Its next inspection is due 43 days later, but it is carried out two days after the due date. On which weekday is the inspection carried out?
questions.explanation: The actual interval is 45 days. Its remainder on division by seven is 3. Advance that many weekdays from Saturday.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Bela and Dev are sisters. The second sister’s husband has a son from an earlier marriage and a daughter with her. What is the first sister’s relationship to that daughter?
questions.explanation: The girl’s mother is the second sister. The mother’s sister is the maternal aunt. The earlier child is unrelated to that identification.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: What is the principal weakness in the owner’s inference?
options: The observed fall can only be explained by customers cancelling appointments.
The start point of the measured interval moved between the two periods.
The shop should compare the price of online and telephone bookings before measuring time.
The statement applies to repair speed but the staff measured the number of available slots.
questions.explanation: The new measurement omits wait time included in the old one. The two figures therefore do not establish a service improvement.
questions.passage: When a repair shop introduced an online booking system, the time recorded between booking and repair fell. Before the change, a customer’s first phone call counted as the start of the wait, even if no appointment was available for days. Afterwards, the clock started only when the customer secured a slot. The owner claimed that the new system made repairs faster. A staff member suggested retaining the new system but measuring from the first attempt to obtain a slot. The change might still be useful, she said, but the existing figures mixed a change in service with a change in what was measured.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Which finding would best support the owner’s claim using the staff member’s proposed method?
options: Time between secured slots and repairs falls again, but first contacts are unrecorded.
The new platform reports shorter times while handling fewer types of repairs.
Several frequent customers say they prefer the online booking interface.
Time from first contact to completed repair falls under comparable demand and job mix.
questions.explanation: A comparable end-to-end measure addresses the shifted start point. Preference or shorter partial intervals do not resolve it.
questions.passage: When a repair shop introduced an online booking system, the time recorded between booking and repair fell. Before the change, a customer’s first phone call counted as the start of the wait, even if no appointment was available for days. Afterwards, the clock started only when the customer secured a slot. The owner claimed that the new system made repairs faster. A staff member suggested retaining the new system but measuring from the first attempt to obtain a slot. The change might still be useful, she said, but the existing figures mixed a change in service with a change in what was measured.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: What does the staff member’s suggestion reveal about her position?
options: She is convinced that the recorded gain came entirely from the changed definition.
She treats the system and the validity of the claim about it as distinct issues.
She wants all customers to return to booking by telephone.
She wants the measurement of waiting replaced by a satisfaction score.
questions.explanation: She explicitly retains the system and changes the measurement.
questions.passage: When a repair shop introduced an online booking system, the time recorded between booking and repair fell. Before the change, a customer’s first phone call counted as the start of the wait, even if no appointment was available for days. Afterwards, the clock started only when the customer secured a slot. The owner claimed that the new system made repairs faster. A staff member suggested retaining the new system but measuring from the first attempt to obtain a slot. The change might still be useful, she said, but the existing figures mixed a change in service with a change in what was measured.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Which example has the same measurement problem?
options: A clinic reports shorter waits after it begins timing from check-in instead of appointment request.
A bus operator reports fewer delays after increasing the time between services.
A library reports longer loans after extending the maximum loan period.
A bakery sells more bread during the same opening hours after adding a second counter.
questions.explanation: The clinic, like the shop, shifts the starting event and leaves out earlier waiting.
questions.passage: When a repair shop introduced an online booking system, the time recorded between booking and repair fell. Before the change, a customer’s first phone call counted as the start of the wait, even if no appointment was available for days. Afterwards, the clock started only when the customer secured a slot. The owner claimed that the new system made repairs faster. A staff member suggested retaining the new system but measuring from the first attempt to obtain a slot. The change might still be useful, she said, but the existing figures mixed a change in service with a change in what was measured.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A machine transforms 18 to 6 and 50 to 10 by replacing an integer with the product of its distinct prime factors. If 144 is passed through the machine, and its output is passed through again, what is the final result?
questions.explanation: The first pass multiplies one copy of each distinct prime to give 6. The second pass sees exactly those same primes, each already present once.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A list ranks higher score first. For tied scores, earlier submission wins. K scores 21 at 09:21, L scores 36 at 09:24, M scores 36 at 09:18, and N scores 21 at 09:14. Two entries from each score band are initially listed. If M’s time is corrected to 09:29, which consecutive pair occupies places 2 and 3, in order?
questions.explanation: L now leads M in the higher-score band. N leads K in the lower-score band. The order is L, M, N, K.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In a queue of 53, H is 14th from the front and J is 18th from the back. They swap places and everyone faces the other way, reversing which end is the front. How many people are ahead of J in the new direction?
questions.explanation: J moves to H’s old position. Under reversal the 39 people formerly behind that slot are now ahead.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In a row of 53, H is 14th from the left and J is 18th from the right, with J right of H. Three people between them leave. Two new people join left of H. How many now stand between H and J?
questions.explanation: J began at position 36 from the left, so the gap contained 21 people. Only the three removals affect that gap.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: H ranks 21st in a preliminary list. The final list removes two people originally above H and adds 9 new entries. Half of the new entries, rounded down to a whole number, are placed ahead of H. What is H’s final rank?
questions.explanation: Remove two higher ranks and add the stated number of newly higher ranks. Removed or added entries below H do not change H’s position.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Six runners have distinct times. S is faster than W but slower than T and P. U is faster than T and P is slower than T. W is faster than V. If the times of T and V are swapped, who is at rank 6, where rank 1 is fastest?
questions.explanation: The original order is U, T, P, S, W, V. The swap gives U, V, P, S, W, T. Read rank 6 from the new order.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In a list of 53, K ranks 14th from the front and L ranks 18th from the rear. M ranks midway between them, counting positions. If there are two middle positions, use the one closer to K. What is M’s rank from the rear?
questions.explanation: L is at position 36 from the front. The lower of the central positions is 25. Convert it to the reverse rank by subtracting from 53 and adding 1.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Find the missing interior term in 9, 11, ?, 23, 39, 71, 135.
questions.explanation: The gaps double: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64. Add 4 to the second term to get 15.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: The six readings are 9, 13, 37, 41, 89, 93. The gaps alternate an unchanged increment with an increasing increment forming an arithmetic progression. What is the sum of the seventh and eighth readings?
questions.explanation: The changing gaps go 24, 48, 72, interleaved with +4. The seventh reading is 165. Add it to the eighth, which is 4 higher.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: One term in 14, 22, 42, 52, 74, 90 was copied incorrectly. For the original sequence, at position n start with n² + 9n, then add 4 on odd positions. Which value needs replacing?
questions.explanation: Calculate the expected values at positions 1 through 6. The value at position 3 should be 40, two less than the listed value.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Each value from the third onward is the sum of the previous two. In the display 9, ?, 19, 29, 48, 77, what value must replace the question mark?
questions.explanation: Subtract the first term 9 from the third term 19. The answer 10 also gives the correct fourth term when added to the third.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A register displays 9, 19, 56, 113, 338, 677 by alternating between two calculation rules. Which value is first to exceed 2029 if the pattern continues?
questions.explanation: Apply ×2 + 1, then ×3 − 1, alternately. The sixth term uses the ×2 rule, so the seventh is 3 × 677 − 1 = 2030.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Complete both blanks in this sequence: 9, 45, 11, 44, 15, 41, __, __.
questions.explanation: Odd positions increase by consecutive even numbers (+2, +4, +6). Even positions decrease by consecutive odd numbers (−1, −3, −5).

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A five-letter code sends DELTA to EGOXF and PLANT to QNDRY. What code does it give FLINT?
questions.explanation: Reading two examples reveals successive shifts +1, +2, +3, +4 and +5. Apply those position shifts to FLINT and wrap after Z.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: On odd positions a code advances the letter by 3. On even positions it uses A↔Z, B↔Y, and so on. Which plain word produces IOLMW?
questions.explanation: Move odd-position letters backward by the stated shift. Mirroring is its own inverse at even positions.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A code transforms DELTA into DQIBG. First it shifts the two end letters forward by 3 and the three inside letters back by 3. What does the same code produce for FLINT, if it then reverses the shifted letters?
questions.explanation: The shifted intermediate word is IIFKW. Its reversal is WKFII.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In a cipher DELTA becomes FDNVZ and GUIDE becomes ITHFD. The rule depends on whether the original letter is a vowel. How is FLINT encoded?
questions.explanation: From the examples, a vowel goes back one letter, and a consonant goes forward two letters. Classify each original letter separately.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: To encode a word, write its last, first and middle letters in that order as alphabet positions (A = 1). Replace each successive number after the first with its sum with the preceding original number. If the result is 20 / 26 / 15, what are the original first, middle and last letters in that order?
questions.explanation: The first displayed number gives the last letter. Subtract it from the second number to recover the first letter. Subtract the recovered first-letter value from the third to recover the middle letter.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Pairs 8 → 36 and 9 → 46 use the same rule. The rule uses the sum of the first n positive numbers, adjusted only when n is odd. Which output is paired with 16?
questions.explanation: An even input gives n(n+1)/2. The odd example is one larger than its triangular number, so add one only when the new input is odd.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: For a two-digit number with unequal digits, 27 corresponds to 45 and 41 corresponds to 27. The output is the positive difference between the number and its reversal. Which input has the same output as 46?
questions.explanation: The difference is nine times the absolute digit gap. 4 and 6 differ by 2; both digits can increase by one without changing that gap.

title: RRB Station Master CBT · Practice model 6
note: Full-length CBT practice with linked data sources, independently keyed constraint puzzles, English comprehension and multi-step mental reasoning. Uses the indicative 30/30/20/20 breakdown.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The water level in a cuboid tank of base 15 cm by 24 cm rises from 7 cm to 13 cm when an object is fully submerged. What is the object’s volume?
questions.explanation: The object displaces the base area multiplied by the rise in water level.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A circular island of radius 7 m is surrounded by a walkway 3 m wide. What is the walkway area, in multiples of π?
questions.explanation: Subtract the inner disk from the outer disk: (r+3)²−r² = 6r+9.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 9 m vertical pole casts a 12 m shadow. From the shadow tip what is the cosine of the angle of elevation?
questions.explanation: The right triangle is a scaled 3–4–5 triangle. Cosine is the horizontal side over the hypotenuse.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A metal sheet measures 15 cm by 25 cm and is 4 mm thick. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: Convert the thickness to 0.4 cm. Multiplying it by the base area gives 10 times the first side length.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 36 cm³ sample of density 3 g/cm³ is combined with a 24 cm³ sample of density 5 g/cm³ without volume change. What is their combined density?
questions.explanation: The mass is 36k+40k = 76k g and the volume is 20k cm³, where k = 3. Divide to obtain the density.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A component has a mass of 8 kg. What is the decrease in weight when moved from a location with g = 10 m/s² to one with g = 8 m/s²?
questions.explanation: Mass stays constant. Weight changes by the mass times the 2 m/s² difference in g.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 8 kg trolley is pulled east by 56 N and west by 32 N. It starts at rest. How far does it travel in 4 s if the forces are constant?
questions.explanation: The net force is 3 times the mass, giving 3 m/s² east. From rest, distance = ½×3×4².

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A sliding crate is pulled with a horizontal force of 75 N along 7 m. Kinetic friction is 25 N. What is the net work on the crate?
questions.explanation: Only horizontal forces do work here. Their net value is twice the friction force in the direction of travel.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 8 kg object slows from 8 m/s to 4 m/s. Find the magnitude of net work done during braking.
questions.explanation: The magnitude of the kinetic energy decrease is ½m(8²−4²) = 24m.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A lift raises a 40 kg load by 3 m in 6 s at a steady speed. Take g = 10 m/s² and efficiency 75%. What input power is needed to the nearest watt?
questions.explanation: Useful power is (5m)×10×3/6 = 125m watts. Divide by 0.75 to find the input power.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 204 N load acts 20 cm to the left of a frictionless pivot. A 34 N load counterbalances it on the right. What is the right-hand lever arm?
questions.explanation: For equilibrium the moments are equal. The smaller force must have 6 times the lever arm.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Resistors of 5 Ω and 10 Ω are connected in series to 30 V. What power is delivered to the larger resistor?
questions.explanation: Total resistance is 15 Ω. The series current is 2 A, so the larger resistor receives I²R = 4×10.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two 10 Ω resistors are connected in parallel to 30 V. One branch opens. How much does the current drawn from the source decrease?
questions.explanation: Each connected branch draws V/R = 3 A. Disconnecting one branch removes its 3 A contribution.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 1.75 kW appliance runs for 48 min each day for 10 days. What is its electricity cost at ₹6.50/kWh?
questions.explanation: Forty-eight minutes is 0.8 hour. Multiply power by 8 hours total and then by ₹6.50/kWh.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Mix 300 g of water at 75°C with 900 g at 15°C in an insulated vessel of negligible heat capacity. What is the equilibrium temperature?
questions.explanation: The cooler water has triple the mass. The weighted mean is (75+3×15)/4.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A heater transfers 2700 J of energy into a 0.3 kg metal block. If the temperature rises by 15°C, find the block’s specific heat capacity.
questions.explanation: Use c=Q/(mΔT), which gives 2700 divided by 0.3×15.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A linear sensor reads 3 units at 0°C and 106 units at 100°C. What is the reading at 40°C, to one decimal place?
questions.explanation: Add 40% of the change from zero to boiling to the sensor’s reading at 0°C.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: An ideal pulley system has four rope segments supporting a 180 N load. What is the work done at the free end to raise the load 1.5 m?
questions.explanation: In an ideal machine the input work equals the increase in potential energy: weight × height.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The ordered measurements are 3, 6, 9, 11, 13, 18, 23. The smallest is corrected to 28. What is the new median?
questions.explanation: The corrected value moves to the end. The old fifth observation becomes the new fourth observation.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A workshop pays a fixed fee of ₹88 plus ₹7 per unit. It pays ₹340 total. What would the bill have been if it had used 6 fewer units?
questions.explanation: The fee is unchanged. Subtract 6×₹7 from the original bill.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two adjacent interior angles of a parallelogram differ by 6°. What is the larger angle?
questions.explanation: Adjacent angles sum to 180°. The larger is 90° plus half their stated difference.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A depot marks a spare part at ₹1400. It applies discounts of 20% and then 15%. What is the sale price?
questions.explanation: Multiply the marked price by 0.8×0.85 = 0.68. The second discount applies to the reduced price.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: After selling 30% of its ticket stock, a depot has 147 tickets. How many would remain if it then sold one-seventh of the remaining tickets?
questions.explanation: The second sale leaves six-sevenths of 147. The original stock is unnecessary for this step.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The mean mass of 16 sacks is 41 kg. Four other sacks averaging 46 kg are added. What is the combined mean to two decimal places?
questions.explanation: Add the two total masses before dividing by the new number of sacks.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: P can complete a task in 18 days and Q in 36 days. They work together for 3 days. How many more days does Q need alone?
questions.explanation: Together they complete k(1/(6k)+1/(12k)) = one-quarter. Q completes the remaining three-quarters in 9k days. Here k = 3.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 144 m train travels at 72 km/h and passes a second train moving towards it at 36 km/h. If the entire pass takes 6 seconds, how long is the second train?
questions.explanation: The combined speed is 30 m/s. Multiply by the passing time to get both lengths together and subtract the length of the first train.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A total of 66 tickets cost ₹2055. Regular tickets cost ₹40 and concession tickets cost ₹25. How many regular tickets were sold?
questions.explanation: Subtract what all concession tickets would cost from the actual total, then divide the difference by ₹15.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A waiting hall has 14 rows. The first row has 13 seats and each subsequent row has 3 more. How many seats are in the last four rows together?
questions.explanation: The last four rows have L, L−3, L−6 and L−9 seats, where L is the final row count.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A status display refreshes every 12 min and a timer every 18 min. Both refresh at 08:00. How many minutes after 08:00 do they refresh together for the third time, excluding 08:00?
questions.explanation: The joint period is LCM(4k,6k) = 12k, with k = 3. The third joint refresh is after three such periods.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: There are 7 red and 10 blue tokens. Two are sampled without replacement. What is the probability of sampling two reds, to three decimals?
questions.explanation: Multiply the probability of a red first by the conditional probability of another red after one has been removed.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: Six evening parcels are diverted from North to East. By how much does the combined spare capacity of North and East change that evening?
questions.explanation: The transfer changes each lane’s occupancy in opposite directions. Their combined arrivals and combined capacity are unchanged.

questions.explanation: Available morning spaces are 22, 13, 22 and 18. Both North and South qualify, but North has the smaller total capacity. Its remaining space is 22 − 19 = 3.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A lamp is already on. Each pulse reverses its state. It receives 19 pulses before a pause, then 17 more pulses. questions.explanation: The total number of automatic toggles is 36. Each pair cancels. The manual toggle then reverses the state once more.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question:
Exactly one of Asha, Bina, Charu is assigned a report, and exactly 1 of the following claims are true.
1. Asha is assigned the report.
2. Asha is not assigned the report.
3. Bina is not assigned the report.
Who receives the report?
questions.explanation: Test the three possible recipients. Assigning the report to Asha makes 2 claims true; assigning it to Bina makes 1 claims true; assigning it to Charu makes 2 claims true. Only Bina yields the required count.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: An audit reviews 40 requests. A request can pass only if both its date and fare are verified. All requests with verified fares have reference codes. Exactly 10 requests lack a code and 12 requests lack date verification. The two groups overlap in two cases. What is the largest possible number of passes?
questions.explanation: Any request without a code lacks fare verification and therefore fails. The union of the two groups is 10 + 12 − 2 = 20 requests. At most 40 − 20 can pass, and that is possible if all other requests meet both requirements.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Five applicants Kiran, Lata, Meena, Nila and Pia are each on at least one of two lists. List X has three names and List Y has three names. X includes Kiran and Lata; Y includes Meena and Nila. Both lists exclude the two names already given for the other list. Who must appear on both?
questions.explanation: The given members are exclusive. The only remaining applicant, Pia, must fill the third place on both lists.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A surveyor starts facing south, goes 17 m forward, turns left and goes 10 m, then turns left again and goes 14 m. Ignoring obstacles, which displacement from the start is correct?
questions.explanation: The first and third walks are opposite, leaving 17 − 14 = 3 m along the original heading. The middle walk is to the left of the starting direction.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Exactly two of Kiran, Lata, Meena and Nila are on leave. Kiran is on leave if and only if Meena is on leave. Nila is working. The two people at work must cover reception and records, one duty each. Nila covers records. Who covers reception?
questions.explanation: Because Nila is working and exactly two people are on leave, the paired leave status must put Kiran and Meena on leave. The working pair is Lata and Nila.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Team P inspected 20 boxes and team Q inspected 10 boxes. Exactly 12 of all inspected boxes were rejected. Each team inspected a disjoint set. What is the minimum possible number of rejections from P?
questions.explanation: At most 10 rejections can come from Q because Q inspected only 10. That leaves at least 2 among P. The minimum is attainable if every Q box was rejected.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A committee selects exactly two of reports Kiran, Lata, Meena and Nila. Selecting Kiran forces Meena. Selecting Nila rules out Meena. New rules also forbid choosing Lata together with Meena, and forbid choosing Lata together with Nila. Which pair can be selected?
questions.explanation: Any pair containing Kiran must also contain Meena. Without Kiran, all three possible pairs among Lata, Meena and Nila breach a prohibition. The single valid pair is Kiran–Meena.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: All express services have reserved coaches. Some night services are express services. No unstaffed service has a reserved coach. Which conclusion follows?

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A bus operator proposes extending a route because most current passengers say they would benefit. Which assumption is needed to infer that most current passengers as a whole support the change from a survey of weekday evening riders?

Rider opinions in the surveyed time window are representative of the relevant wider ridership.
The survey asked every driver to vote on the proposal.
Passengers who support the change will travel a strictly higher number of trips.
questions.explanation: The sample covers a time window. A claim about the entire group requires the sampled riders’ opinions to generalise beyond it.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Asha and Bina are sisters. The second sister’s husband has a son from an earlier marriage and a daughter with her. What is the first sister’s relationship to that daughter?

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: What trade-off does the illustrator accept?
options: A simpler image can make unresolved evidence easier to distinguish.
A busier image can make the evidence behind the reconstruction easier to evaluate.
Dotted edges make the fossil easier to identify but harder to compare with other species.
A detailed illustration must sacrifice clarity to include all competing reconstructions.
questions.explanation: The revised visual is harder to scan immediately, but easier to evaluate because it distinguishes evidence from inference.
questions.passage: A scientific illustrator was asked to draw a fossil from fragments. A clean outline made it easy to see the animal’s general shape, but viewers interpreted every line as something actually preserved. She revised the drawing so that preserved edges were solid and inferred edges dotted. Some readers found the result visually busier. The illustrator agreed, but argued that a drawing could be both attractive and misleading if it concealed the degree of reconstruction. An illustration that communicates uncertainty may be slower to read on first viewing yet quicker to use when comparing competing reconstructions.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Why did readers misunderstand the first drawing?
options: The fragments showed two incompatible types of outer edge.
Readers assumed that dotted lines identified the largest preserved pieces.
The illustrator used a different scale for each fragment.
The same visual convention was used for preserved and inferred boundaries.
questions.explanation: A solid outline communicated a uniform level of certainty that the fragments did not support.
questions.passage: A scientific illustrator was asked to draw a fossil from fragments. questions.question: What function does the final sentence serve?
options: It proposes a faster way to reconstruct the fossil fragments.
It argues that readers should see only one drawing at a time.
It separates quick visual recognition from efficient comparison of evidence.
It asserts that competing drawings must have been made from different fossils.
questions.explanation: The sentence contrasts two kinds of speed, first viewing and a later evidence comparison.

options: Use one boundary style everywhere to make a map easier to copy.
Remove a scale bar from a map so that the area appears less crowded.
Show surveyed boundaries with one line style and estimated boundaries with another.
Colour each part of an illustration by size while leaving reconstruction uncertain.
questions.explanation: Distinguishing surveyed from estimated boundaries makes the status of each claim visible.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: H ranks 22nd in a preliminary list. The final list removes two people originally above H and adds 10 new entries. Half of the new entries, rounded down to a whole number, are placed ahead of H. What is H’s final rank?
questions.explanation: Remove two higher ranks and add the stated number of newly higher ranks. Removed or added entries below H do not change H’s position.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Six runners have distinct times. S is faster than W but slower than T and P. U is faster than T and P is slower than T. W is faster than V. If the times of P and V are swapped, who is at rank 1, where rank 1 is fastest?
questions.explanation: The original order is U, T, P, S, W, V. The swap gives U, T, V, S, W, P. Read rank 1 from the new order.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In a list of 56, K ranks 15th from the front and L ranks 19th from the rear. M ranks midway between them, counting positions. If there are two middle positions, use the one closer to K. What is M’s rank from the rear?
questions.explanation: L is at position 38 from the front. The lower of the central positions is 26. Convert it to the reverse rank by subtracting from 56 and adding 1.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A list ranks higher score first. For tied scores, earlier submission wins. K scores 22 at 09:21, L scores 38 at 09:24, M scores 38 at 09:18, and N scores 22 at 09:14. Two entries from each score band are initially listed. If M’s time is corrected to 09:29, which consecutive pair occupies places 2 and 3, in order?
questions.explanation: L now leads M in the higher-score band. N leads K in the lower-score band. The order is L, M, N, K.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: The six readings are 10, 15, 29, 34, 62, 67. The gaps alternate an unchanged increment with an increasing increment forming an arithmetic progression. What is the sum of the seventh and eighth readings?
questions.explanation: The changing gaps go 14, 28, 42, interleaved with +5. The seventh reading is 109. Add it to the eighth, which is 5 higher.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: One term in 16, 24, 44, 58, 80, 96 was copied incorrectly. For the original sequence, at position n start with n² + 10n, then add 5 on odd positions. Which value needs replacing?
questions.explanation: Calculate the expected values at positions 1 through 6. The value at position 4 should be 56, two less than the listed value.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Each value from the third onward is the sum of the previous two. In the display 10, ?, 21, 32, 53, 85, what value must replace the question mark?
questions.explanation: Subtract the first term 10 from the third term 21. The answer 11 also gives the correct fourth term when added to the third.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A register displays 10, 21, 62, 125, 374, 749 by alternating between two calculation rules. Which value is first to exceed 2245 if the pattern continues?
questions.explanation: Apply ×2 + 1, then ×3 − 1, alternately. The sixth term uses the ×2 rule, so the seventh is 3 × 749 − 1 = 2246.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Complete both blanks in this sequence: 10, 50, 12, 49, 16, 46, __, __.
questions.explanation: Odd positions increase by consecutive even numbers (+2, +4, +6). Even positions decrease by consecutive odd numbers (−1, −3, −5).

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Find the missing interior term in 10, 12, ?, 24, 40, 72, 136.
questions.explanation: The gaps double: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64. Add 4 to the second term to get 16.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: On odd positions a code advances the letter by 1. On even positions it uses A↔Z, B↔Y, and so on. Which plain word produces HIPEF?
questions.explanation: Move odd-position letters backward by the stated shift. Mirroring is its own inverse at even positions.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A code transforms EMBER into SDALF. First it shifts the two end letters forward by 1 and the three inside letters back by 1. What does the same code produce for GROVE, if it then reverses the shifted letters?
questions.explanation: The shifted intermediate word is HQNUF. Its reversal is FUNQH.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In a cipher EMBER becomes DODDT and GUIDE becomes ITHFD. The rule depends on whether the original letter is a vowel. How is GROVE encoded?
questions.explanation: From the examples, a vowel goes back one letter, and a consonant goes forward two letters. Classify each original letter separately.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: To encode a word, write its last, first and middle letters in that order as alphabet positions (A = 1). Replace each successive number after the first with its sum with the preceding original number. If the result is 5 / 12 / 22, what are the original first, middle and last letters in that order?
questions.explanation: The first displayed number gives the last letter. Subtract it from the second number to recover the first letter. Subtract the recovered first-letter value from the third to recover the middle letter.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A five-letter code sends EMBER to FOEIW and PLANT to QNDRY. What code does it give GROVE?
questions.explanation: Reading two examples reveals successive shifts +1, +2, +3, +4 and +5. Apply those position shifts to GROVE and wrap after Z.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: For a two-digit number with unequal digits, 27 corresponds to 45 and 41 corresponds to 27. The output is the positive difference between the number and its reversal. Which input has the same output as 27?
questions.explanation: The difference is nine times the absolute digit gap. 2 and 7 differ by 5; both digits can increase by one without changing that gap.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In each pair (p,q) value one place apart gives (4,5) → 9 and (7,8) → 15. Check also (5,8) → 39. Under the same relation, what is (13,16)?
questions.explanation: The relation is q² − p² = (q − p)(q + p). The three-unit gap multiplies the sum of the two entries.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: The rule sends 4 to 17, 7 to 47, and 9 to 77. It multiplies each input by one less than itself and adds a fixed constant. Which input gives 77?
questions.explanation: The examples establish the constant as 5. Subtract it from the target, then identify the adjacent factors. The larger factor is the input.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A machine transforms 18 to 6 and 50 to 10 by replacing an integer with the product of its distinct prime factors. If 156 is passed through the machine, and its output is passed through again, what is the final result?
questions.explanation: The first pass multiplies one copy of each distinct prime to give 78. The second pass sees exactly those same primes, each already present once.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Pairs 9 → 46 and 10 → 55 use the same rule. The rule uses the sum of the first n positive numbers, adjusted only when n is odd. Which output is paired with 17?
questions.explanation: An even input gives n(n+1)/2. The odd example is one larger than its triangular number, so add one only when the new input is odd.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A metal sheet measures 16 cm by 25 cm and is 4 mm thick. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: Convert the thickness to 0.4 cm. Multiplying it by the base area gives 10 times the first side length.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 48 cm³ sample of density 3 g/cm³ is combined with a 32 cm³ sample of density 5 g/cm³ without volume change. What is their combined density?
questions.explanation: The mass is 36k+40k = 76k g and the volume is 20k cm³, where k = 4. Divide to obtain the density.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A component has a mass of 9 kg. What is the decrease in weight when moved from a location with g = 10 m/s² to one with g = 8 m/s²?
questions.explanation: Mass stays constant. Weight changes by the mass times the 2 m/s² difference in g.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 9 kg trolley is pulled east by 63 N and west by 36 N. It starts at rest. How far does it travel in 4 s if the forces are constant?
questions.explanation: The net force is 3 times the mass, giving 3 m/s² east. From rest, distance = ½×3×4².

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A sliding crate is pulled with a horizontal force of 90 N along 8 m. Kinetic friction is 30 N. What is the net work on the crate?
questions.explanation: Only horizontal forces do work here. Their net value is twice the friction force in the direction of travel.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 9 kg object slows from 8 m/s to 4 m/s. Find the magnitude of net work done during braking.
questions.explanation: The magnitude of the kinetic energy decrease is ½m(8²−4²) = 24m.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A lift raises a 45 kg load by 3 m in 6 s at a steady speed. Take g = 10 m/s² and efficiency 75%. What input power is needed to the nearest watt?
questions.explanation: Useful power is (5m)×10×3/6 = 125m watts. Divide by 0.75 to find the input power.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 245 N load acts 20 cm to the left of a frictionless pivot. A 35 N load counterbalances it on the right. What is the right-hand lever arm?
questions.explanation: For equilibrium the moments are equal. The smaller force must have 7 times the lever arm.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Resistors of 6 Ω and 12 Ω are connected in series to 36 V. What power is delivered to the larger resistor?
questions.explanation: Total resistance is 18 Ω. The series current is 2 A, so the larger resistor receives I²R = 4×12.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two 12 Ω resistors are connected in parallel to 36 V. One branch opens. How much does the current drawn from the source decrease?
questions.explanation: Each connected branch draws V/R = 3 A. Disconnecting one branch removes its 3 A contribution.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 2 kW appliance runs for 48 min each day for 10 days. What is its electricity cost at ₹6.50/kWh?
questions.explanation: Forty-eight minutes is 0.8 hour. Multiply power by 8 hours total and then by ₹6.50/kWh.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Mix 400 g of water at 75°C with 1200 g at 15°C in an insulated vessel of negligible heat capacity. What is the equilibrium temperature?
questions.explanation: The cooler water has triple the mass. The weighted mean is (75+3×15)/4.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A heater transfers 3600 J of energy into a 0.4 kg metal block. If the temperature rises by 15°C, find the block’s specific heat capacity.
questions.explanation: Use c=Q/(mΔT), which gives 3600 divided by 0.4×15.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A linear sensor reads 4 units at 0°C and 108 units at 100°C. What is the reading at 40°C, to one decimal place?
questions.explanation: Add 40% of the change from zero to boiling to the sensor’s reading at 0°C.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: An ideal pulley system has four rope segments supporting a 240 N load. What is the work done at the free end to raise the load 1.5 m?
questions.explanation: In an ideal machine the input work equals the increase in potential energy: weight × height.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The ordered measurements are 4, 7, 10, 12, 14, 19, 24. The smallest is corrected to 29. What is the new median?
questions.explanation: The corrected value moves to the end. The old fifth observation becomes the new fourth observation.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A workshop pays a fixed fee of ₹89 plus ₹7 per unit. It pays ₹355 total. What would the bill have been if it had used 6 fewer units?
questions.explanation: The fee is unchanged. Subtract 6×₹7 from the original bill.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two adjacent interior angles of a parallelogram differ by 8°. What is the larger angle?
questions.explanation: Adjacent angles sum to 180°. The larger is 90° plus half their stated difference.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A depot marks a spare part at ₹1500. It applies discounts of 20% and then 15%. What is the sale price?
questions.explanation: Multiply the marked price by 0.8×0.85 = 0.68. The second discount applies to the reduced price.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: After selling 30% of its ticket stock, a depot has 154 tickets. How many would remain if it then sold one-seventh of the remaining tickets?
questions.explanation: The second sale leaves six-sevenths of 154. The original stock is unnecessary for this step.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The mean mass of 18 sacks is 41 kg. Four other sacks averaging 47 kg are added. What is the combined mean to two decimal places?
questions.explanation: Add the two total masses before dividing by the new number of sacks.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: P can complete a task in 24 days and Q in 48 days. They work together for 4 days. How many more days does Q need alone?
questions.explanation: Together they complete k(1/(6k)+1/(12k)) = one-quarter. Q completes the remaining three-quarters in 9k days. Here k = 4.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 168 m train travels at 72 km/h and passes a second train moving towards it at 36 km/h. If the entire pass takes 7 seconds, how long is the second train?
questions.explanation: The combined speed is 30 m/s. Multiply by the passing time to get both lengths together and subtract the length of the first train.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A total of 78 tickets cost ₹2430. Regular tickets cost ₹40 and concession tickets cost ₹25. How many regular tickets were sold?
questions.explanation: Subtract what all concession tickets would cost from the actual total, then divide the difference by ₹15.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A waiting hall has 16 rows. The first row has 13 seats and each subsequent row has 3 more. How many seats are in the last four rows together?
questions.explanation: The last four rows have L, L−3, L−6 and L−9 seats, where L is the final row count.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A status display refreshes every 16 min and a timer every 24 min. Both refresh at 08:00. How many minutes after 08:00 do they refresh together for the third time, excluding 08:00?
questions.explanation: The joint period is LCM(4k,6k) = 12k, with k = 4. The third joint refresh is after three such periods.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: There are 8 red and 11 blue tokens. Two are sampled without replacement. What is the probability of sampling two reds, to three decimals?
questions.explanation: Multiply the probability of a red first by the conditional probability of another red after one has been removed.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The water level in a cuboid tank of base 20 cm by 24 cm rises from 7 cm to 14 cm when an object is fully submerged. What is the object’s volume?
questions.explanation: The object displaces the base area multiplied by the rise in water level.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A circular island of radius 8 m is surrounded by a walkway 3 m wide. What is the walkway area, in multiples of π?
questions.explanation: Subtract the inner disk from the outer disk: (r+3)²−r² = 6r+9.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 12 m vertical pole casts a 16 m shadow. From the shadow tip what is the cosine of the angle of elevation?
questions.explanation: The right triangle is a scaled 3–4–5 triangle. Cosine is the horizontal side over the hypotenuse.

questions.explanation: Available morning spaces are 22, 13, 22 and 18. Both North and South qualify, but North has the smaller total capacity. Its remaining space is 22 − 19 = 3.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question:
Exactly one of Farah, Gita, Hema is assigned a report, and exactly 1 of the following claims are true.
1. Farah is assigned the report.
2. Farah is not assigned the report.
3. Hema is not assigned the report.
Who receives the report?
questions.explanation: Test the three possible recipients. Assigning the report to Farah makes 2 claims true; assigning it to Gita makes 2 claims true; assigning it to Hema makes 1 claims true. Only Hema yields the required count.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: An audit reviews 44 requests. A request can pass only if both its date and fare are verified. All requests with verified fares have reference codes. Exactly 11 requests lack a code and 13 requests lack date verification. The two groups overlap in two cases. What is the largest possible number of passes?
questions.explanation: Any request without a code lacks fare verification and therefore fails. The union of the two groups is 11 + 13 − 2 = 22 requests. At most 44 − 22 can pass, and that is possible if all other requests meet both requirements.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A parcel is held if it is unlabelled or exceeds the mass limit. A particular parcel was not held. What must be true under this rule?
options: It is labelled or over the mass limit.
It is within the limit but unlabelled.
It has been accepted for delivery.
It is labelled and within the mass limit.
questions.explanation: Either listed condition would trigger holding. Not being held rules out both, without establishing acceptance.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A surveyor starts facing north, goes 18 m forward, turns left and goes 11 m, then turns left again and goes 15 m. Ignoring obstacles, which displacement from the start is correct?
questions.explanation: The first and third walks are opposite, leaving 18 − 15 = 3 m along the original heading. The middle walk is to the left of the starting direction.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: P is true only if Q is true. R is true exactly when Q is false. If R is true, which truth values are forced for P and Q?
questions.explanation: R being true forces Q false. Since P requires Q, P must also be false.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Team P inspected 22 boxes and team Q inspected 11 boxes. Exactly 13 of all inspected boxes were rejected. Each team inspected a disjoint set. What is the minimum possible number of rejections from P?
questions.explanation: At most 11 rejections can come from Q because Q inspected only 11. That leaves at least 2 among P. The minimum is attainable if every Q box was rejected.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: What is the smaller angle between the hands of a clock at 4:40?
questions.explanation: The minute hand is at 240° and the hour hand at 120°+20° = 140°. Their difference is 100°.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: If 1 January of a leap year is a Monday, what weekday is 1 March that year?
questions.explanation: January and February supply 31+29 = 60 days. The shift is four weekdays.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: An archive introduced an optional guide to help visitors locate maps. Which finding most strongly supports the claim that the guide reduces the time spent searching?
options: Frequent visitors use the guide more often and are also faster searchers.
Randomly assigned guide users locate the same maps faster than non-users.
Downloads rise after signs pointing to the archive are installed.
Most guide users say the maps were accurately catalogued.
questions.explanation: A randomised comparison using the same tasks reduces pre-existing differences and measures the relevant outcome.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Which order satisfies every clue, from position 1 to position 5?
questions.explanation: Checking the stated restrictions leaves only Hema → Jaya → Gita → Indu → Farah. Farah → Hema → Gita → Indu → Jaya violates clue 2. Farah → Hema → Gita → Jaya → Indu violates clue 2. Gita → Hema → Farah → Indu → Jaya violates clue 1.

4. Jaya is not immediately to the left of Farah.
5. Indu sits to the right of Hema.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: If clue 1 is dropped and all other clues still apply, how many orders are possible?
questions.explanation: Retain all clues except 1. The remaining constraints admit 18 distinct permutations, including the original order. Count arrangements with position 1 fixed before moving to the next permitted first item.
