questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Between 2:00 and the first overlap after it, when is the smaller angle between the clock hands 32.5°?
questions.explanation: On this side of the overlap the separation is 30 × 2 − 5.5m. Set that equal to 32.5 and solve for m = 5.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A register is inspected on a Monday. Its next inspection is due 49 days later, but it is carried out two days after the due date. On which weekday is the inspection carried out?
questions.explanation: The actual interval is 51 days. Its remainder on division by seven is 2. Advance that many weekdays from Monday.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: M is the sister of N. N is the father of P. Q is P’s son. How is M related to Q?
questions.explanation: M is the sister of Q’s grandfather, so she is Q’s grand-aunt.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Five containers weigh 11, 13, 16, 20, 26 kg. A loading bay accepts exactly two whose combined weight is exactly 37 kg. The heavier selected container is loaded first. Which weight is loaded second?
questions.explanation: Testing pairs against the capacity leaves 26 + 11 = 37. In descending weight order the second is 11 kg.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A lamp is already on. Each pulse reverses its state. It receives 22 pulses before a pause, then 20 more pulses. During maintenance the technician manually toggles it once and disconnects it before any further pulse. What was its state immediately before the manual toggle and immediately afterwards?
questions.explanation: The total number of automatic toggles is 42. Each pair cancels. The manual toggle then reverses the state once more.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: What justifies the committee’s decision most directly?
options: Every later repair reverses some damage caused by the earliest known dial.
A reconstruction to the oldest appearance would be impossible because the clock no longer works.
The clock’s successive alterations are historical evidence and the earliest appearance is uncertain.
The committee values the collector’s original condition but cannot fund it.
questions.explanation: The passage gives both a limit on reconstructing the first state and a reason to preserve later layers.
questions.passage: A collector offered to fund the restoration of a market clock if the town promised to return it to its first recorded appearance. Restoration workers discovered a painted dial behind the metal face and several layers of repairs. The earliest illustration was imprecise, and later changes showed how different generations had maintained the clock. The municipal committee decided to preserve the readable face, expose part of the older dial through a display panel, and document the uncertain dates. Its report argued that a single reconstructed appearance would be more familiar to visitors but would communicate a weaker account of the object’s history.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Which claim about the committee is supported by the passage?
options: It concluded that the painted dial must be older than any recorded appearance.
It designed its policy to draw more visitors to the market.
It rejected displaying any part of the original dial until the exact date was known.
It balanced readability, retained evidence and uncertainty about historical dates.
questions.explanation: The readable face, partial display and documentation each meet one of these three considerations.
questions.passage: A collector offered to fund the restoration of a market clock if the town promised to return it to its first recorded appearance. Restoration workers discovered a painted dial behind the metal face and several layers of repairs. The earliest illustration was imprecise, and later changes showed how different generations had maintained the clock. The municipal committee decided to preserve the readable face, expose part of the older dial through a display panel, and document the uncertain dates. Its report argued that a single reconstructed appearance would be more familiar to visitors but would communicate a weaker account of the object’s history.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: What would most weaken the claim that only the earliest appearance is historically informative?
options: The town has another clock manufactured in the same century.
A later repair is found to reveal a distinctive maintenance method no longer documented elsewhere.
The collector can fund a team to copy the earliest known illustration.
Several visitors say they find the oldest design easier to recognise.
questions.explanation: Unique evidence captured by a later repair shows why later states can have independent historical value.
questions.passage: A collector offered to fund the restoration of a market clock if the town promised to return it to its first recorded appearance. Restoration workers discovered a painted dial behind the metal face and several layers of repairs. The earliest illustration was imprecise, and later changes showed how different generations had maintained the clock. The municipal committee decided to preserve the readable face, expose part of the older dial through a display panel, and document the uncertain dates. Its report argued that a single reconstructed appearance would be more familiar to visitors but would communicate a weaker account of the object’s history.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Which sentence would fit the committee’s report?
options: Because the first illustration is incomplete, later repairs cannot be dated or interpreted.
Showing several stages can explain the object’s use even when its first appearance remains uncertain.
A complete reconstruction is justified whenever visitors recognise it quickly.
Historical value rises in direct proportion to the age of each visible part.
questions.explanation: The report presents the clock’s history as several recoverable stages, without treating the first as fully known.
questions.passage: A collector offered to fund the restoration of a market clock if the town promised to return it to its first recorded appearance. Restoration workers discovered a painted dial behind the metal face and several layers of repairs. The earliest illustration was imprecise, and later changes showed how different generations had maintained the clock. The municipal committee decided to preserve the readable face, expose part of the older dial through a display panel, and document the uncertain dates. Its report argued that a single reconstructed appearance would be more familiar to visitors but would communicate a weaker account of the object’s history.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In a queue of 59, H is 16th from the front and J is 20th from the back. They swap places and everyone faces the other way, reversing which end is the front. How many people are ahead of J in the new direction?
questions.explanation: J moves to H’s old position. Under reversal the 43 people formerly behind that slot are now ahead.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: One term in 18, 26, 48, 60, 88, 102 was copied incorrectly. For the original sequence, at position n start with n² + 11n, then add 6 on odd positions. Which value needs replacing?
questions.explanation: Calculate the expected values at positions 1 through 6. The value at position 5 should be 86, two less than the listed value.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Each value from the third onward is the sum of the previous two. In the display 11, ?, 23, 35, 58, 93, what value must replace the question mark?
questions.explanation: Subtract the first term 11 from the third term 23. The answer 12 also gives the correct fourth term when added to the third.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A register displays 11, 23, 68, 137, 410, 821 by alternating between two calculation rules. Which value is first to exceed 2461 if the pattern continues?
questions.explanation: Apply ×2 + 1, then ×3 − 1, alternately. The sixth term uses the ×2 rule, so the seventh is 3 × 821 − 1 = 2462.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Complete both blanks in this sequence: 11, 55, 13, 54, 17, 51, __, __.
questions.explanation: Odd positions increase by consecutive even numbers (+2, +4, +6). Even positions decrease by consecutive odd numbers (−1, −3, −5).

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Find the missing interior term in 11, 13, ?, 25, 41, 73, 137.
questions.explanation: The gaps double: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64. Add 4 to the second term to get 17.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: The six readings are 11, 17, 33, 39, 71, 77. The gaps alternate an unchanged increment with an increasing increment forming an arithmetic progression. What is the sum of the seventh and eighth readings?
questions.explanation: The changing gaps go 16, 32, 48, interleaved with +6. The seventh reading is 125. Add it to the eighth, which is 6 higher.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A code transforms RAINY into ALGYT. First it shifts the two end letters forward by 2 and the three inside letters back by 2. What does the same code produce for PLUME, if it then reverses the shifted letters?
questions.explanation: The shifted intermediate word is RJSKG. Its reversal is GKSJR.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In a cipher RAINY becomes TZHPA and GUIDE becomes ITHFD. The rule depends on whether the original letter is a vowel. How is PLUME encoded?
questions.explanation: From the examples, a vowel goes back one letter, and a consonant goes forward two letters. Classify each original letter separately.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: To encode a word, write its last, first and middle letters in that order as alphabet positions (A = 1). Replace each successive number after the first with its sum with the preceding original number. If the result is 5 / 21 / 37, what are the original first, middle and last letters in that order?
questions.explanation: The first displayed number gives the last letter. Subtract it from the second number to recover the first letter. Subtract the recovered first-letter value from the third to recover the middle letter.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A five-letter code sends RAINY to SCLRD and PLANT to QNDRY. What code does it give PLUME?
questions.explanation: Reading two examples reveals successive shifts +1, +2, +3, +4 and +5. Apply those position shifts to PLUME and wrap after Z.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: On odd positions a code advances the letter by 2. On even positions it uses A↔Z, B↔Y, and so on. Which plain word produces ROWNG?
questions.explanation: Move odd-position letters backward by the stated shift. Mirroring is its own inverse at even positions.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In each pair (p,q) value one place apart gives (4,5) → 9 and (7,8) → 15. Check also (5,8) → 39. Under the same relation, what is (14,17)?
questions.explanation: The relation is q² − p² = (q − p)(q + p). The three-unit gap multiplies the sum of the two entries.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: The rule sends 4 to 17, 7 to 47, and 9 to 77. It multiplies each input by one less than itself and adds a fixed constant. Which input gives 95?
questions.explanation: The examples establish the constant as 5. Subtract it from the target, then identify the adjacent factors. The larger factor is the input.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A machine transforms 18 to 6 and 50 to 10 by replacing an integer with the product of its distinct prime factors. If 168 is passed through the machine, and its output is passed through again, what is the final result?
questions.explanation: The first pass multiplies one copy of each distinct prime to give 42. The second pass sees exactly those same primes, each already present once.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Pairs 10 → 55 and 11 → 67 use the same rule. The rule uses the sum of the first n positive numbers, adjusted only when n is odd. Which output is paired with 18?
questions.explanation: An even input gives n(n+1)/2. The odd example is one larger than its triangular number, so add one only when the new input is odd.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: For a two-digit number with unequal digits, 27 corresponds to 45 and 41 corresponds to 27. The output is the positive difference between the number and its reversal. Which input has the same output as 38?
questions.explanation: The difference is nine times the absolute digit gap. 3 and 8 differ by 5; both digits can increase by one without changing that gap.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In a row of 59, H is 16th from the left and J is 20th from the right, with J right of H. Three people between them leave. Two new people join left of H. How many now stand between H and J?
questions.explanation: J began at position 40 from the left, so the gap contained 23 people. Only the three removals affect that gap.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: H ranks 23rd in a preliminary list. The final list removes two people originally above H and adds 11 new entries. Half of the new entries, rounded down to a whole number, are placed ahead of H. What is H’s final rank?
questions.explanation: Remove two higher ranks and add the stated number of newly higher ranks. Removed or added entries below H do not change H’s position.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Six runners have distinct times. S is faster than W but slower than T and P. U is faster than T and P is slower than T. W is faster than V. If the times of S and V are swapped, who is at rank 2, where rank 1 is fastest?
questions.explanation: The original order is U, T, P, S, W, V. The swap gives U, T, P, V, W, S. Read rank 2 from the new order.

title: RRB Station Master CBT · Practice model 8
note: Full-length CBT practice with linked data sources, independently keyed constraint puzzles, English comprehension and multi-step mental reasoning. Uses the indicative 30/30/20/20 breakdown.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 10 kg trolley is pulled east by 70 N and west by 40 N. It starts at rest. How far does it travel in 4 s if the forces are constant?
questions.explanation: The net force is 3 times the mass, giving 3 m/s² east. From rest, distance = ½×3×4².

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A sliding crate is pulled with a horizontal force of 105 N along 9 m. Kinetic friction is 35 N. What is the net work on the crate?
questions.explanation: Only horizontal forces do work here. Their net value is twice the friction force in the direction of travel.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 10 kg object slows from 8 m/s to 4 m/s. Find the magnitude of net work done during braking.
questions.explanation: The magnitude of the kinetic energy decrease is ½m(8²−4²) = 24m.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A lift raises a 50 kg load by 3 m in 6 s at a steady speed. Take g = 10 m/s² and efficiency 75%. What input power is needed to the nearest watt?
questions.explanation: Useful power is (5m)×10×3/6 = 125m watts. Divide by 0.75 to find the input power.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 288 N load acts 20 cm to the left of a frictionless pivot. A 36 N load counterbalances it on the right. What is the right-hand lever arm?
questions.explanation: For equilibrium the moments are equal. The smaller force must have 8 times the lever arm.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Resistors of 7 Ω and 14 Ω are connected in series to 42 V. What power is delivered to the larger resistor?
questions.explanation: Total resistance is 21 Ω. The series current is 2 A, so the larger resistor receives I²R = 4×14.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two 14 Ω resistors are connected in parallel to 42 V. One branch opens. How much does the current drawn from the source decrease?
questions.explanation: Each connected branch draws V/R = 3 A. Disconnecting one branch removes its 3 A contribution.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 2.25 kW appliance runs for 48 min each day for 10 days. What is its electricity cost at ₹6.50/kWh?
questions.explanation: Forty-eight minutes is 0.8 hour. Multiply power by 8 hours total and then by ₹6.50/kWh.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Mix 500 g of water at 75°C with 1500 g at 15°C in an insulated vessel of negligible heat capacity. What is the equilibrium temperature?
questions.explanation: The cooler water has triple the mass. The weighted mean is (75+3×15)/4.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A heater transfers 4500 J of energy into a 0.5 kg metal block. If the temperature rises by 15°C, find the block’s specific heat capacity.
questions.explanation: Use c=Q/(mΔT), which gives 4500 divided by 0.5×15.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A linear sensor reads 5 units at 0°C and 110 units at 100°C. What is the reading at 40°C, to one decimal place?
questions.explanation: Add 40% of the change from zero to boiling to the sensor’s reading at 0°C.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: An ideal pulley system has four rope segments supporting a 300 N load. What is the work done at the free end to raise the load 1.5 m?
questions.explanation: In an ideal machine the input work equals the increase in potential energy: weight × height.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The ordered measurements are 5, 8, 11, 13, 15, 20, 25. The smallest is corrected to 30. What is the new median?
questions.explanation: The corrected value moves to the end. The old fifth observation becomes the new fourth observation.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A workshop pays a fixed fee of ₹90 plus ₹7 per unit. It pays ₹370 total. What would the bill have been if it had used 6 fewer units?
questions.explanation: The fee is unchanged. Subtract 6×₹7 from the original bill.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two adjacent interior angles of a parallelogram differ by 10°. What is the larger angle?
questions.explanation: Adjacent angles sum to 180°. The larger is 90° plus half their stated difference.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A depot marks a spare part at ₹1600. It applies discounts of 20% and then 15%. What is the sale price?
questions.explanation: Multiply the marked price by 0.8×0.85 = 0.68. The second discount applies to the reduced price.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: After selling 30% of its ticket stock, a depot has 161 tickets. How many would remain if it then sold one-seventh of the remaining tickets?
questions.explanation: The second sale leaves six-sevenths of 161. The original stock is unnecessary for this step.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The mean mass of 20 sacks is 41 kg. Four other sacks averaging 48 kg are added. What is the combined mean to two decimal places?
questions.explanation: Add the two total masses before dividing by the new number of sacks.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: P can complete a task in 30 days and Q in 60 days. They work together for 5 days. How many more days does Q need alone?
questions.explanation: Together they complete k(1/(6k)+1/(12k)) = one-quarter. Q completes the remaining three-quarters in 9k days. Here k = 5.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 192 m train travels at 72 km/h and passes a second train moving towards it at 36 km/h. If the entire pass takes 8 seconds, how long is the second train?
questions.explanation: The combined speed is 30 m/s. Multiply by the passing time to get both lengths together and subtract the length of the first train.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A total of 90 tickets cost ₹2805. Regular tickets cost ₹40 and concession tickets cost ₹25. How many regular tickets were sold?
questions.explanation: Subtract what all concession tickets would cost from the actual total, then divide the difference by ₹15.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A waiting hall has 18 rows. The first row has 13 seats and each subsequent row has 3 more. How many seats are in the last four rows together?
questions.explanation: The last four rows have L, L−3, L−6 and L−9 seats, where L is the final row count.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A status display refreshes every 20 min and a timer every 30 min. Both refresh at 08:00. How many minutes after 08:00 do they refresh together for the third time, excluding 08:00?
questions.explanation: The joint period is LCM(4k,6k) = 12k, with k = 5. The third joint refresh is after three such periods.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: There are 9 red and 12 blue tokens. Two are sampled without replacement. What is the probability of sampling two reds, to three decimals?
questions.explanation: Multiply the probability of a red first by the conditional probability of another red after one has been removed.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The water level in a cuboid tank of base 25 cm by 24 cm rises from 7 cm to 15 cm when an object is fully submerged. What is the object’s volume?
questions.explanation: The object displaces the base area multiplied by the rise in water level.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A circular island of radius 9 m is surrounded by a walkway 3 m wide. What is the walkway area, in multiples of π?
questions.explanation: Subtract the inner disk from the outer disk: (r+3)²−r² = 6r+9.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 15 m vertical pole casts a 20 m shadow. From the shadow tip what is the cosine of the angle of elevation?
questions.explanation: The right triangle is a scaled 3–4–5 triangle. Cosine is the horizontal side over the hypotenuse.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A metal sheet measures 17 cm by 25 cm and is 4 mm thick. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: Convert the thickness to 0.4 cm. Multiplying it by the base area gives 10 times the first side length.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 60 cm³ sample of density 3 g/cm³ is combined with a 40 cm³ sample of density 5 g/cm³ without volume change. What is their combined density?
questions.explanation: The mass is 36k+40k = 76k g and the volume is 20k cm³, where k = 5. Divide to obtain the density.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A component has a mass of 10 kg. What is the decrease in weight when moved from a location with g = 10 m/s² to one with g = 8 m/s²?
questions.explanation: Mass stays constant. Weight changes by the mass times the 2 m/s² difference in g.

questions.question: By how much can Q’s received amount vary across all permissible splits if both depots must receive at least two boxes, with no additional minimum?
questions.explanation: Q can receive from 2 up to 58. Neither capacity binds. The difference between the extremes is 56.
questions.table:
Boxes sent to P and Q before reallocation
Depot | Opening capacity
P | 72
Q | 75
Shared overnight stock | 60
The shared stock is split in whole boxes. The capacity limits apply to the overnight split.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: How many boxes went to P? Statement I: P received six more boxes than Q. Statement II: Q received fewer boxes than P.
options: Statement II alone determines the split.
Both statements are needed to determine the split.
Statement I alone determines the split.
Even together the statements leave more than one split.
questions.explanation: Together with P+Q = 60, the exact difference gives P = 33 and Q = 27. A comparison without a difference is insufficient.
questions.table:

Depot | Opening capacity
P | 72
Q | 75
Shared overnight stock | 60
The shared stock is split in whole boxes. The capacity limits apply to the overnight split.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: If each depot must receive at least one third of the overnight stock, rounded up, how many more boxes can one depot receive than the other at most?
questions.explanation: To maximise the gap, give one depot the smallest permissible allocation, 20, and the other the rest. Subtract the smaller allocation from the larger.
questions.table:

Depot | Opening capacity
P | 72
Q | 75
Shared overnight stock | 60
The shared stock is split in whole boxes. The capacity limits apply to the overnight split.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: Counters P and Q sold 160 tickets together. How many did P sell? I. P sold 10 more than Q. II. P sold more than 40 tickets.
questions.explanation: The total and exact difference determine P. A lower bound alone leaves several possible counts.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: A service by Eluru has a total of 340 seats in two coaches. How many seats does coach A have? I. A has more seats than B. II. B has exactly 125 seats.
questions.explanation: Subtract the known B count from the total. Knowing only which is larger does not determine the count.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: An audit reviews 48 requests. A request can pass only if both its date and fare are verified. All requests with verified fares have reference codes. Exactly 12 requests lack a code and 14 requests lack date verification. The two groups overlap in two cases. What is the largest possible number of passes?
questions.explanation: Any request without a code lacks fare verification and therefore fails. The union of the two groups is 12 + 14 − 2 = 24 requests. At most 48 − 24 can pass, and that is possible if all other requests meet both requirements.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A notice asks passengers to use the west entrance during repairs. Which assumption is necessary for that instruction to be workable?
options: Every passenger enters from the west each day.
Passengers can reach the west entrance during the repairs.
Repairs will finish before the next train arrives.
The west entrance has the lowest footfall at all times.
questions.explanation: An instruction to use that entrance presupposes it can be reached. The other conditions are unnecessary.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A surveyor starts facing south, goes 19 m forward, turns left and goes 12 m, then turns left again and goes 16 m. Ignoring obstacles, which displacement from the start is correct?
questions.explanation: The first and third walks are opposite, leaving 19 − 16 = 3 m along the original heading. The middle walk is to the left of the starting direction.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Platform signs were revised and queries to the help desk fell. Which additional finding best supports the claim that the signs helped people find platforms?
options: The drop was in direction queries at stations with revised signs, while comparable unchanged stations saw no drop.
All help desks shortened opening hours on the same date.
The number of passengers fell sharply at every station.
Queries about refunds fell, but direction queries stayed the same.
questions.explanation: The targeted decrease and comparison group support a link to the signs more directly than other changes do.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Team P inspected 24 boxes and team Q inspected 12 boxes. Exactly 14 of all inspected boxes were rejected. Each team inspected a disjoint set. What is the minimum possible number of rejections from P?
questions.explanation: At most 12 rejections can come from Q because Q inspected only 12. That leaves at least 2 among P. The minimum is attainable if every Q box was rejected.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Exactly two of A, B, C and D are selected. A and B cannot both be selected. Selecting C requires D. Which pair is impossible?
questions.explanation: A and C would require a third selection, D. The other listed pairs meet both constraints.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Exactly one of Arun, Bela and Charan took a file. Arun says “Bela took it.” Bela says “Charan did not take it.” Charan says “Arun did not take it.” Exactly one statement is true. Who took the file?
questions.explanation: If Arun took it, only Bela’s statement is true. If Charan took it, only Charan’s is true. Bela taking it would make all three true.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Every service is classified as delayed or on time. No delayed service was assigned platform 1. Some services assigned platform 1 were express. Which conclusion follows?
options: Some express services were on time.
No on-time service used a different platform.
questions.explanation: The platform 1 expresses cannot be delayed. Under the two-way classification they were on time.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Which order satisfies every clue, from position 1 to position 5?
questions.explanation: Checking the stated restrictions leaves only Packing → Mapping → Labelling → Dispatch → Weighing. Mapping → Weighing → Labelling → Packing → Dispatch violates clue 1. Mapping → Weighing → Labelling → Dispatch → Packing violates clue 1. Mapping → Weighing → Packing → Labelling → Dispatch violates clue 1.
questions.passage:
Five activities occupy successive slots, one per slot, with no breaks between slots.
1. Mapping immediately follows Packing, and Weighing immediately follows Dispatch.
2. Labelling is earlier than Dispatch but later than Mapping.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: If clue 1 is dropped and all other clues still apply, how many orders are possible?
questions.explanation: Retain all clues except 1. The remaining constraints admit 3 distinct permutations, including the original order. Count arrangements with position 1 fixed before moving to the next permitted first item.
questions.passage:
Five interviews take place on Monday through Friday, one per day. Positions 1–5 are Monday–Friday.
1. Lata is interviewed immediately before Nila.
2. Meena is interviewed two days before Lata.
3. Pia is interviewed after Meena but before Lata.
4. Kiran is earlier than Meena.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Between 3:00 and the first overlap after it, when is the smaller angle between the clock hands 13°?
questions.explanation: On this side of the overlap the separation is 30 × 3 − 5.5m. Set that equal to 13 and solve for m = 14.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A register is inspected on a Tuesday. Its next inspection is due 52 days later, but it is carried out two days after the due date. On which weekday is the inspection carried out?
questions.explanation: The actual interval is 54 days. Its remainder on division by seven is 5. Advance that many weekdays from Tuesday.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Which statement negates “Every parcel is checked and labelled”?
options: Every parcel is unchecked and unlabelled.
At least one parcel is checked and labelled.
No parcel is checked unless it is labelled.
At least one parcel is unchecked or unlabelled.
questions.explanation: One parcel failing either requirement is sufficient to make the universal statement false.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Five containers weigh 12, 14, 17, 21, 27 kg. A loading bay accepts exactly two whose combined weight is exactly 39 kg. The heavier selected container is loaded first. Which weight is loaded second?
questions.explanation: Testing pairs against the capacity leaves 27 + 12 = 39. In descending weight order the second is 12 kg.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A lamp is already on. Each pulse reverses its state. It receives 25 pulses before a pause, then 19 more pulses. During maintenance the technician manually toggles it once and disconnects it before any further pulse. What was its state immediately before the manual toggle and immediately afterwards?
questions.explanation: The total number of automatic toggles is 44. Each pair cancels. The manual toggle then reverses the state once more.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question:
Exactly one of Kiran, Lata, Meena is assigned a report, and exactly 3 of the following claims are true.
1. Kiran is assigned the report.
2. Lata is not assigned the report.
3. Meena is not assigned the report.
Who receives the report?
questions.explanation: Test the three possible recipients. Assigning the report to Kiran makes 3 claims true; assigning it to Lata makes 1 claims true; assigning it to Meena makes 1 claims true. Only Kiran yields the required count.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: What explains why the figures can differ without either being wrong?
options: One agency measured in a district while the other omitted its own area.
The figures were gathered using different units that cannot be compared.
Both agencies made independent estimates of exactly the same quantity.
They describe water at different points, and some volume may be held between measurements.
questions.explanation: Intake and delivery are different measured volumes. Storage can also shift delivery across reporting periods.
questions.passage: Two water agencies reported different results for a canal. The first measured volume entering a district; the second measured volume delivered to fields. Their figures were initially presented as contradictory. A canal engineer pointed out that the agencies were counting at different points in the same system. Some of the gap came from storage changes and evaporation, but not all storage changes were recorded. She proposed aligning the measurement dates before estimating losses. Otherwise, water held overnight might be counted as lost in one report and as delivered in the next.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Which information would best help distinguish loss from temporary storage?
options: A record of how many fields normally use the canal each season.
Readings of canal storage at the start and end of a common reporting interval.
The two agencies’ annual operating budgets.
The average travel distance from the agency offices to the canal.
questions.explanation: Change in stored volume over aligned dates helps explain the part of the flow gap that is not lost.
questions.passage: Two water agencies reported different results for a canal. The first measured volume entering a district; the second measured volume delivered to fields. Their figures were initially presented as contradictory. A canal engineer pointed out that the agencies were counting at different points in the same system. Some of the gap came from storage changes and evaporation, but not all storage changes were recorded. She proposed aligning the measurement dates before estimating losses. Otherwise, water held overnight might be counted as lost in one report and as delivered in the next.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: What role does the overnight example play?
options: It proves that evaporation is negligible after sunset.
It identifies a defect in the field delivery instrument.
It illustrates how a timing mismatch can create an apparent loss.
It quantifies the share of the gap explained by storage.
questions.explanation: The example describes possible treatment of the same water in consecutive reporting windows.
questions.passage: Two water agencies reported different results for a canal. The first measured volume entering a district; the second measured volume delivered to fields. Their figures were initially presented as contradictory. A canal engineer pointed out that the agencies were counting at different points in the same system. Some of the gap came from storage changes and evaporation, but not all storage changes were recorded. She proposed aligning the measurement dates before estimating losses. Otherwise, water held overnight might be counted as lost in one report and as delivered in the next.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Where should the engineer begin if aligning measurement dates changes little?
options: Conclude the agencies measured identical quantities after all.
Investigate the remaining difference using storage records and other loss estimates.
Ignore the remaining difference because only timing can affect flow.
Compare district population figures to determine which report is correct.
questions.explanation: A small timing effect does not eliminate other explanations. It leaves a gap to be investigated.
questions.passage: Two water agencies reported different results for a canal. The first measured volume entering a district; the second measured volume delivered to fields. Their figures were initially presented as contradictory. A canal engineer pointed out that the agencies were counting at different points in the same system. Some of the gap came from storage changes and evaporation, but not all storage changes were recorded. She proposed aligning the measurement dates before estimating losses. Otherwise, water held overnight might be counted as lost in one report and as delivered in the next.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Complete both blanks in this sequence: 12, 60, 14, 59, 18, 56, __, __.
questions.explanation: Odd positions increase by consecutive even numbers (+2, +4, +6). Even positions decrease by consecutive odd numbers (−1, −3, −5).

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Find the missing interior term in 12, 14, ?, 26, 42, 74, 138.
questions.explanation: The gaps double: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64. Add 4 to the second term to get 18.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: The six readings are 12, 15, 33, 36, 72, 75. The gaps alternate an unchanged increment with an increasing increment forming an arithmetic progression. What is the sum of the seventh and eighth readings?
questions.explanation: The changing gaps go 18, 36, 54, interleaved with +3. The seventh reading is 129. Add it to the eighth, which is 3 higher.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: One term in 16, 30, 48, 64, 88, 108 was copied incorrectly. For the original sequence, at position n start with n² + 12n, then add 3 on odd positions. Which value needs replacing?
questions.explanation: Calculate the expected values at positions 1 through 6. The value at position 2 should be 28, two less than the listed value.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In a cipher HONEY becomes JNPDA and GUIDE becomes ITHFD. The rule depends on whether the original letter is a vowel. How is STONE encoded?
questions.explanation: From the examples, a vowel goes back one letter, and a consonant goes forward two letters. Classify each original letter separately.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: To encode a word, write its last, first and middle letters in that order as alphabet positions (A = 1). Replace each successive number after the first with its sum with the preceding original number. If the result is 5 / 24 / 34, what are the original first, middle and last letters in that order?
questions.explanation: The first displayed number gives the last letter. Subtract it from the second number to recover the first letter. Subtract the recovered first-letter value from the third to recover the middle letter.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A five-letter code sends HONEY to IQQID and PLANT to QNDRY. What code does it give STONE?
questions.explanation: Reading two examples reveals successive shifts +1, +2, +3, +4 and +5. Apply those position shifts to STONE and wrap after Z.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: On odd positions a code advances the letter by 3. On even positions it uses A↔Z, B↔Y, and so on. Which plain word produces VGRMH?
questions.explanation: Move odd-position letters backward by the stated shift. Mirroring is its own inverse at even positions.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A code transforms HONEY into BBKLK. First it shifts the two end letters forward by 3 and the three inside letters back by 3. What does the same code produce for STONE, if it then reverses the shifted letters?
questions.explanation: The shifted intermediate word is VQLKH. Its reversal is HKLQV.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: The rule sends 4 to 17, 7 to 47, and 9 to 77. It multiplies each input by one less than itself and adds a fixed constant. Which input gives 115?
questions.explanation: The examples establish the constant as 5. Subtract it from the target, then identify the adjacent factors. The larger factor is the input.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A machine transforms 18 to 6 and 50 to 10 by replacing an integer with the product of its distinct prime factors. If 180 is passed through the machine, and its output is passed through again, what is the final result?
questions.explanation: The first pass multiplies one copy of each distinct prime to give 30. The second pass sees exactly those same primes, each already present once.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Pairs 11 → 67 and 12 → 78 use the same rule. The rule uses the sum of the first n positive numbers, adjusted only when n is odd. Which output is paired with 19?
questions.explanation: An even input gives n(n+1)/2. The odd example is one larger than its triangular number, so add one only when the new input is odd.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: For a two-digit number with unequal digits, 27 corresponds to 45 and 41 corresponds to 27. The output is the positive difference between the number and its reversal. Which input has the same output as 45?
questions.explanation: The difference is nine times the absolute digit gap. 4 and 5 differ by 1; both digits can increase by one without changing that gap.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In each pair (p,q) value one place apart gives (4,5) → 9 and (7,8) → 15. Check also (5,8) → 39. Under the same relation, what is (15,18)?
questions.explanation: The relation is q² − p² = (q − p)(q + p). The three-unit gap multiplies the sum of the two entries.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: H ranks 24th in a preliminary list. The final list removes two people originally above H and adds 12 new entries. Half of the new entries, rounded down to a whole number, are placed ahead of H. What is H’s final rank?
questions.explanation: Remove two higher ranks and add the stated number of newly higher ranks. Removed or added entries below H do not change H’s position.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Six runners have distinct times. S is faster than W but slower than T and P. U is faster than T and P is slower than T. W is faster than V. If the times of U and W are swapped, who is at rank 3, where rank 1 is fastest?
questions.explanation: The original order is U, T, P, S, W, V. The swap gives W, T, P, S, U, V. Read rank 3 from the new order.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In a list of 62, K ranks 17th from the front and L ranks 21st from the rear. M ranks midway between them, counting positions. If there are two middle positions, use the one closer to K. What is M’s rank from the rear?
questions.explanation: L is at position 42 from the front. The lower of the central positions is 29. Convert it to the reverse rank by subtracting from 62 and adding 1.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A list ranks higher score first. For tied scores, earlier submission wins. K scores 24 at 09:21, L scores 42 at 09:24, M scores 42 at 09:18, and N scores 24 at 09:14. Two entries from each score band are initially listed. If M’s time is corrected to 09:29, which consecutive pair occupies places 2 and 3, in order?
questions.explanation: L now leads M in the higher-score band. N leads K in the lower-score band. The order is L, M, N, K.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In a queue of 62, H is 17th from the front and J is 21st from the back. They swap places and everyone faces the other way, reversing which end is the front. How many people are ahead of J in the new direction?
questions.explanation: J moves to H’s old position. Under reversal the 45 people formerly behind that slot are now ahead.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In a row of 62, H is 17th from the left and J is 21st from the right, with J right of H. Three people between them leave. Two new people join left of H. How many now stand between H and J?
questions.explanation: J began at position 42 from the left, so the gap contained 24 people. Only the three removals affect that gap.

title: RRB Station Master CBT · Practice model 9
note: Full-length CBT practice with linked data sources, independently keyed constraint puzzles, English comprehension and multi-step mental reasoning. Uses the indicative 30/30/20/20 breakdown.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A lift raises a 55 kg load by 3 m in 6 s at a steady speed. Take g = 10 m/s² and efficiency 75%. What input power is needed to the nearest watt?
questions.explanation: Useful power is (5m)×10×3/6 = 125m watts. Divide by 0.75 to find the input power.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 333 N load acts 20 cm to the left of a frictionless pivot. A 37 N load counterbalances it on the right. What is the right-hand lever arm?
questions.explanation: For equilibrium the moments are equal. The smaller force must have 9 times the lever arm.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Resistors of 8 Ω and 16 Ω are connected in series to 48 V. What power is delivered to the larger resistor?
questions.explanation: Total resistance is 24 Ω. The series current is 2 A, so the larger resistor receives I²R = 4×16.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two 16 Ω resistors are connected in parallel to 48 V. One branch opens. How much does the current drawn from the source decrease?
questions.explanation: Each connected branch draws V/R = 3 A. Disconnecting one branch removes its 3 A contribution.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 2.5 kW appliance runs for 48 min each day for 10 days. What is its electricity cost at ₹6.50/kWh?
questions.explanation: Forty-eight minutes is 0.8 hour. Multiply power by 8 hours total and then by ₹6.50/kWh.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Mix 600 g of water at 75°C with 1800 g at 15°C in an insulated vessel of negligible heat capacity. What is the equilibrium temperature?
questions.explanation: The cooler water has triple the mass. The weighted mean is (75+3×15)/4.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A heater transfers 5400 J of energy into a 0.6 kg metal block. If the temperature rises by 15°C, find the block’s specific heat capacity.
questions.explanation: Use c=Q/(mΔT), which gives 5400 divided by 0.6×15.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A linear sensor reads 6 units at 0°C and 112 units at 100°C. What is the reading at 40°C, to one decimal place?
questions.explanation: Add 40% of the change from zero to boiling to the sensor’s reading at 0°C.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: An ideal pulley system has four rope segments supporting a 360 N load. What is the work done at the free end to raise the load 1.5 m?
questions.explanation: In an ideal machine the input work equals the increase in potential energy: weight × height.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The ordered measurements are 6, 9, 12, 14, 16, 21, 26. The smallest is corrected to 31. What is the new median?
questions.explanation: The corrected value moves to the end. The old fifth observation becomes the new fourth observation.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A workshop pays a fixed fee of ₹91 plus ₹7 per unit. It pays ₹385 total. What would the bill have been if it had used 6 fewer units?
questions.explanation: The fee is unchanged. Subtract 6×₹7 from the original bill.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two adjacent interior angles of a parallelogram differ by 12°. What is the larger angle?
questions.explanation: Adjacent angles sum to 180°. The larger is 90° plus half their stated difference.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A depot marks a spare part at ₹1700. It applies discounts of 20% and then 15%. What is the sale price?
questions.explanation: Multiply the marked price by 0.8×0.85 = 0.68. The second discount applies to the reduced price.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: After selling 30% of its ticket stock, a depot has 168 tickets. How many would remain if it then sold one-seventh of the remaining tickets?
questions.explanation: The second sale leaves six-sevenths of 168. The original stock is unnecessary for this step.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The mean mass of 22 sacks is 41 kg. Four other sacks averaging 49 kg are added. What is the combined mean to two decimal places?
questions.explanation: Add the two total masses before dividing by the new number of sacks.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: P can complete a task in 36 days and Q in 72 days. They work together for 6 days. How many more days does Q need alone?
questions.explanation: Together they complete k(1/(6k)+1/(12k)) = one-quarter. Q completes the remaining three-quarters in 9k days. Here k = 6.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 216 m train travels at 72 km/h and passes a second train moving towards it at 36 km/h. If the entire pass takes 9 seconds, how long is the second train?
questions.explanation: The combined speed is 30 m/s. Multiply by the passing time to get both lengths together and subtract the length of the first train.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A total of 102 tickets cost ₹3180. Regular tickets cost ₹40 and concession tickets cost ₹25. How many regular tickets were sold?
questions.explanation: Subtract what all concession tickets would cost from the actual total, then divide the difference by ₹15.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A waiting hall has 20 rows. The first row has 13 seats and each subsequent row has 3 more. How many seats are in the last four rows together?
questions.explanation: The last four rows have L, L−3, L−6 and L−9 seats, where L is the final row count.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A status display refreshes every 24 min and a timer every 36 min. Both refresh at 08:00. How many minutes after 08:00 do they refresh together for the third time, excluding 08:00?
questions.explanation: The joint period is LCM(4k,6k) = 12k, with k = 6. The third joint refresh is after three such periods.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: There are 10 red and 13 blue tokens. Two are sampled without replacement. What is the probability of sampling two reds, to three decimals?
questions.explanation: Multiply the probability of a red first by the conditional probability of another red after one has been removed.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The water level in a cuboid tank of base 30 cm by 24 cm rises from 7 cm to 16 cm when an object is fully submerged. What is the object’s volume?
questions.explanation: The object displaces the base area multiplied by the rise in water level.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A circular island of radius 10 m is surrounded by a walkway 3 m wide. What is the walkway area, in multiples of π?
questions.explanation: Subtract the inner disk from the outer disk: (r+3)²−r² = 6r+9.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 18 m vertical pole casts a 24 m shadow. From the shadow tip what is the cosine of the angle of elevation?
questions.explanation: The right triangle is a scaled 3–4–5 triangle. Cosine is the horizontal side over the hypotenuse.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A metal sheet measures 18 cm by 25 cm and is 4 mm thick. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: Convert the thickness to 0.4 cm. Multiplying it by the base area gives 10 times the first side length.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 72 cm³ sample of density 3 g/cm³ is combined with a 48 cm³ sample of density 5 g/cm³ without volume change. What is their combined density?
questions.explanation: The mass is 36k+40k = 76k g and the volume is 20k cm³, where k = 6. Divide to obtain the density.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A component has a mass of 11 kg. What is the decrease in weight when moved from a location with g = 10 m/s² to one with g = 8 m/s²?
questions.explanation: Mass stays constant. Weight changes by the mass times the 2 m/s² difference in g.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 11 kg trolley is pulled east by 77 N and west by 44 N. It starts at rest. How far does it travel in 4 s if the forces are constant?
questions.explanation: The net force is 3 times the mass, giving 3 m/s² east. From rest, distance = ½×3×4².

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A sliding crate is pulled with a horizontal force of 120 N along 10 m. Kinetic friction is 40 N. What is the net work on the crate?
questions.explanation: Only horizontal forces do work here. Their net value is twice the friction force in the direction of travel.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 11 kg object slows from 8 m/s to 4 m/s. Find the magnitude of net work done during braking.
questions.explanation: The magnitude of the kinetic energy decrease is ½m(8²−4²) = 24m.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: What percentage of the combined East and West capacity is used on the evening shift, to one decimal place?
questions.explanation: Use the two relevant lanes only. Evening arrivals total 73 and the combined capacity is 110.

questions.question: Six evening parcels are diverted from North to East. By how much does the combined spare capacity of North and East change that evening?
questions.explanation: The transfer changes each lane’s occupancy in opposite directions. Their combined arrivals and combined capacity are unchanged.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: How many of the late group D trains must become on time for group D to reach 90% punctuality?
questions.explanation: At 90% punctuality at most 23 group D departures can be late. Subtract this limit from the current 40.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A lamp lights when exactly one of switches P and Q is closed. The lamp is dark while Q is open. What must be true?

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A surveyor starts facing north, goes 20 m forward, turns left and goes 13 m, then turns left again and goes 17 m. Ignoring obstacles, which displacement from the start is correct?
questions.explanation: The first and third walks are opposite, leaving 20 − 17 = 3 m along the original heading. The middle walk is to the left of the starting direction.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: When between 2:00 and 3:00 do the clock hands first coincide?
questions.explanation: The hour hand starts 60° ahead. The minute hand gains 5.5° per minute. The time required is 60/5.5 = 120/11 minutes.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Team P inspected 26 boxes and team Q inspected 13 boxes. Exactly 15 of all inspected boxes were rejected. Each team inspected a disjoint set. What is the minimum possible number of rejections from P?
questions.explanation: At most 13 rejections can come from Q because Q inspected only 13. That leaves at least 2 among P. The minimum is attainable if every Q box was rejected.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: In a non-leap year 1 February falls on Friday. What day is 1 May?
questions.explanation: The February, March and April lengths sum to 28+31+30 = 89 days. The remainder modulo 7 is five, shifting Friday to Wednesday.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Asha is the mother of siblings Bhanu and Chitra. Dev is Chitra’s son and Esha is Bhanu’s daughter. How are Dev and Esha related?
questions.explanation: Their parents are siblings, so they are first cousins.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A depot opts to add an online timetable to reduce calls asking when services leave. Which assumption is necessary for this reasoning?
options: Some callers can access the timetable instead of calling.
Every caller owns the same type of phone.
The depot will abolish telephone support.
Call volumes never change for other reasons.
questions.explanation: To replace some timetable calls, the online service needs to be usable by at least some of those callers.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A register is inspected on a Wednesday. Its next inspection is due 55 days later, but it is carried out two days after the due date. On which weekday is the inspection carried out?

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A pilot programme claims that a new sign cut walking time to exits. Which fact most weakens the claim?
options: The sign used a new font and larger lettering.

A temporary shortcut opened alongside the new sign and closed after the pilot.
Some passengers used an exit on the opposite side.
questions.explanation: A shortcut introduced at the same time could cut walking time without the sign having any effect.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Five containers weigh 13, 15, 18, 22, 28 kg. A loading bay accepts exactly two whose combined weight is exactly 41 kg. The heavier selected container is loaded first. Which weight is loaded second?

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A lamp is already on. Each pulse reverses its state. It receives 28 pulses before a pause, then 22 more pulses. During maintenance the technician manually toggles it once and disconnects it before any further pulse. What was its state immediately before the manual toggle and immediately afterwards?
questions.explanation: The total number of automatic toggles is 50. Each pair cancels. The manual toggle then reverses the state once more.

questions.subject: Logical Capability

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: An audit reviews 52 requests. A request can pass only if both its date and fare are verified. All requests with verified fares have reference codes. Exactly 13 requests lack a code and 15 requests lack date verification. The two groups overlap in two cases. What is the largest possible number of passes?
questions.explanation: Any request without a code lacks fare verification and therefore fails. The union of the two groups is 13 + 15 − 2 = 26 requests. At most 52 − 26 can pass, and that is possible if all other requests meet both requirements.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Why does Arun cross out “always”?
options: The ferryman’s newer route did not use water colour at any point.
Arun has decided that his note should record only the bus journey.
The rule is helpful under some conditions and has a stated exception.
He discovers that the pale water always indicated a deeper stretch.
questions.explanation: The ferryman explains that the colour cue may be unreliable after rain.
questions.passage: On the last day before a bridge reopened, Arun chose the old ferry even though the bus was faster. He had spent years watching the ferryman determine the crossing point by the water’s colour. This time Arun asked for an explanation and learned that pale water near the bank often marked a shallower stretch, though the sign became unreliable after rain. He wrote down the rule on the bus ride home, then crossed out the word always. The note was shorter than his memory of the journey and more useful than the version he had first intended to keep.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Which development gives the story its main change in perspective?
options: A slow trip convinces Arun that the bridge should remain closed.
A familiar action becomes an explicit rule whose limits Arun can describe.
A chance encounter makes Arun choose the ferry for the first time.
A dispute leads Arun to reject a lesson learned from the ferryman.
questions.explanation: Arun moves from observing a habit to understanding the rule and its limits.
questions.passage: On the last day before a bridge reopened, Arun chose the old ferry even though the bus was faster. questions.question: How does the reopening frame the story?
options: It establishes the technical reason for shallow water near the bank.
It suggests that the ferry operated primarily when rain made roads unsafe.
It shows that the bus ride introduced Arun to the ferryman’s method.
It gives urgency to learning a skill tied to a routine that is ending.
questions.explanation: The imminent change makes this a last opportunity to ask about a long-observed practice.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Which description of the note is best supported?
options: It is a compressed account of the practical lesson with a qualification.
It is a transcript that preserves all of the ferryman’s explanation.
It is an unqualified rule that becomes clearer by dropping detail.
It is a record of why a ferry is faster than a bus near the bridge.
questions.explanation: The final note is short, but it keeps the important limit by removing the claim of universality.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Each value from the third onward is the sum of the previous two. In the display 13, ?, 27, 41, 68, 109, what value must replace the question mark?
questions.explanation: Subtract the first term 13 from the third term 27. The answer 14 also gives the correct fourth term when added to the third.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: To encode a word, write its last, first and middle letters in that order as alphabet positions (A = 1). Replace each successive number after the first with its sum with the preceding original number. If the result is 12 / 32 / 21, what are the original first, middle and last letters in that order?
questions.explanation: The first displayed number gives the last letter. Subtract it from the second number to recover the first letter. Subtract the recovered first-letter value from the third to recover the middle letter.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A five-letter code sends VAULT to WCXPY and PLANT to QNDRY. What code does it give TRAIL?
questions.explanation: Reading two examples reveals successive shifts +1, +2, +3, +4 and +5. Apply those position shifts to TRAIL and wrap after Z.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: On odd positions a code advances the letter by 1. On even positions it uses A↔Z, B↔Y, and so on. Which plain word produces UIBRM?
questions.explanation: Move odd-position letters backward by the stated shift. Mirroring is its own inverse at even positions.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A code transforms VAULT into UKTZW. First it shifts the two end letters forward by 1 and the three inside letters back by 1. What does the same code produce for TRAIL, if it then reverses the shifted letters?
questions.explanation: The shifted intermediate word is UQZHM. Its reversal is MHZQU.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In a cipher VAULT becomes XZTNV and GUIDE becomes ITHFD. The rule depends on whether the original letter is a vowel. How is TRAIL encoded?
questions.explanation: From the examples, a vowel goes back one letter, and a consonant goes forward two letters. Classify each original letter separately.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A machine transforms 18 to 6 and 50 to 10 by replacing an integer with the product of its distinct prime factors. If 192 is passed through the machine, and its output is passed through again, what is the final result?
questions.explanation: The first pass multiplies one copy of each distinct prime to give 6. The second pass sees exactly those same primes, each already present once.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Pairs 12 → 78 and 13 → 92 use the same rule. The rule uses the sum of the first n positive numbers, adjusted only when n is odd. Which output is paired with 20?
questions.explanation: An even input gives n(n+1)/2. The odd example is one larger than its triangular number, so add one only when the new input is odd.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: For a two-digit number with unequal digits, 27 corresponds to 45 and 41 corresponds to 27. The output is the positive difference between the number and its reversal. Which input has the same output as 26?
questions.explanation: The difference is nine times the absolute digit gap. 2 and 6 differ by 4; both digits can increase by one without changing that gap.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In each pair (p,q) value one place apart gives (4,5) → 9 and (7,8) → 15. Check also (5,8) → 39. Under the same relation, what is (16,19)?
questions.explanation: The relation is q² − p² = (q − p)(q + p). The three-unit gap multiplies the sum of the two entries.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: The rule sends 4 to 17, 7 to 47, and 9 to 77. It multiplies each input by one less than itself and adds a fixed constant. Which input gives 137?
questions.explanation: The examples establish the constant as 5. Subtract it from the target, then identify the adjacent factors. The larger factor is the input.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Six runners have distinct times. S is faster than W but slower than T and P. U is faster than T and P is slower than T. W is faster than V. If the times of T and W are swapped, who is at rank 4, where rank 1 is fastest?
questions.explanation: The original order is U, T, P, S, W, V. The swap gives U, W, P, S, T, V. Read rank 4 from the new order.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In a list of 65, K ranks 18th from the front and L ranks 22nd from the rear. M ranks midway between them, counting positions. If there are two middle positions, use the one closer to K. What is M’s rank from the rear?
questions.explanation: L is at position 44 from the front. The lower of the central positions is 31. Convert it to the reverse rank by subtracting from 65 and adding 1.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A list ranks higher score first. For tied scores, earlier submission wins. K scores 25 at 09:21, L scores 44 at 09:24, M scores 44 at 09:18, and N scores 25 at 09:14. Two entries from each score band are initially listed. If M’s time is corrected to 09:29, which consecutive pair occupies places 2 and 3, in order?
questions.explanation: L now leads M in the higher-score band. N leads K in the lower-score band. The order is L, M, N, K.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In a queue of 65, H is 18th from the front and J is 22nd from the back. They swap places and everyone faces the other way, reversing which end is the front. How many people are ahead of J in the new direction?
questions.explanation: J moves to H’s old position. Under reversal the 47 people formerly behind that slot are now ahead.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In a row of 65, H is 18th from the left and J is 22nd from the right, with J right of H. Three people between them leave. Two new people join left of H. How many now stand between H and J?
questions.explanation: J began at position 44 from the left, so the gap contained 25 people. Only the three removals affect that gap.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: H ranks 25th in a preliminary list. The final list removes two people originally above H and adds 13 new entries. Half of the new entries, rounded down to a whole number, are placed ahead of H. What is H’s final rank?
questions.explanation: Remove two higher ranks and add the stated number of newly higher ranks. Removed or added entries below H do not change H’s position.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A register displays 13, 27, 80, 161, 482, 965 by alternating between two calculation rules. Which value is first to exceed 2893 if the pattern continues?
questions.explanation: Apply ×2 + 1, then ×3 − 1, alternately. The sixth term uses the ×2 rule, so the seventh is 3 × 965 − 1 = 2894.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Complete both blanks in this sequence: 13, 65, 15, 64, 19, 61, __, __.
questions.explanation: Odd positions increase by consecutive even numbers (+2, +4, +6). Even positions decrease by consecutive odd numbers (−1, −3, −5).

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Find the missing interior term in 13, 15, ?, 27, 43, 75, 139.
questions.explanation: The gaps double: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64. Add 4 to the second term to get 19.
